targeting_gate.verbatim_anchor:
The aim of this study was therefore to assess the effect of tree cover on two soil properties
closely linked to groundwater recharge, namely, inﬁltrability and preferential ﬂow, in an agroforestry park-
land in semiarid Burkina Faso (West Africa). We hypothesized that: (a) preferential ﬂow and soil inﬁltrability
are highest next to trees; (b) in open areas among tree canopies, preferential ﬂow and soil inﬁltrability
decrease with increasing size of the open area, that is, with increasing distance to the nearest tree stem; (c)
termite mounds associated with trees further increase preferential ﬂow and soil inﬁltrability near the trees.
targeting_gate.rationale: Research estimates tree effects on infiltration/preferential flow, not where agroforestry should be implemented. Spatial sampling transects and soil measurements are not siting criteria.
